findings.text: done-when case 2 asserts that a disposed blocking finding starts no round, but `blocking_findings` (`reckon/crew/repair.py:225-240`) already filters `disposition != "open"`, `blocking_finding_dispositions` already reports it, `dispatch_repair_for_run` already records `decline-only` with reason "every blocking finding was disposed", and `tests/test_a_disposed_finding_ends_its_repair_round.py:150-170` already asserts exactly that, so the case passes on the unfixed code and measures nothing

findings.reason: the count is the whole of the reported harm ("found 3 blocking finding(s)" for three non-blocking findings), so a test that does not pin the count lets the node land the same misdescription in a new wording.
findings.text: the deliverable requires that the advice name an unclassified finding "rather than counting it among the blocking findings", but done-when case 5 asserts only that "the advice names it unclassified"; an implementation that appends the word while leaving the count at `len(findings)` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:551`, where `findings` is `compose_repair_node`'s blocking list and includes the unclassified finding) passes every stated case

findings.reason: the fix as written splits the severity decision across two readers, so the worker either lands a half-fix that leaves the same prefixed findings withholding landing, or edits a module its write scope does not grant.
findings.text: the mechanism reads the `blocking:`/`non-blocking:` prefix inside `_finding_kind` (`reckon/crew/repair.py:198-217`), but `declared_severity` (`reckon/crew/review.py:176-192`) is documented as "the one reader of a stored finding's severity, so the promotion audit, the repair reflex and the parser cannot disagree", and it is what `recovery_review_acceptance._finding_blocks` reads to decide whether a finding withholds the run's landing; a prefix read added only in `repair.py` makes the incident's record non-blocking to the reflex and still blocking to the landing gate, and `reckon/crew/review.py` is not among §25's write paths

findings.reason: promotion reads its gate receipt from a log whose path and closing `EXIT=` line the section never asks for, so the node can satisfy every stated case while leaving no artifact a later reader or page promotion gate can open.
findings.text: §25 says "Ruff adds no findings on the staged paths" and names its test, but nothing in it says where the gate log is written, what its first line carries, or that its last line is `EXIT=`, while the plan's other 22 sections each carry "Every log is under the run directory, starts with its revision and the literal command, and ends in `EXIT=`" (verified: 22 occurrences of that sentence, none in §25)
